results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

results.quote: Neighboring chapters own the machinery this chapter regulates.
results.finding: Declared relationship is contrast: from the records the laws ask for (p03) to who owns the machinery behind them, 'so this chapter states obligations rather than rebuilding it'. The paragraph opens with a flat statement, never expresses the contrast or the consequence for this chapter, and re-names the same two chapters p03 just named, so it reads as repetition (flow reader B, item B5).

results.draft_locus: Vertical Differences in Legal Exposure (section position)
results.quote: Across the group and across every rule in this chapter, not only the listing fields of Vertical Rules, verticals weigh the same laws differently
results.finding: Both flow readers mark the section's position 'unclear': a recap of exposure by vertical sits between Trade-offs and Failure Modes, far from Vertical Rules, and interrupts the Trade-offs to Failure Modes to Chief Architect's View run. Reader A: 'It reads as a book-template section. It comes after Trade-offs and well away from Vertical Rules'. The difficulty comes from the declared grouping order itself.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader B, Vertical Differences marked unclear (item B11)

results.quote: Across the group and across every rule in this chapter, not only the listing fields of Vertical Rules, verticals weigh the same laws differently, differ most in listing rules, and enter DAC7 only when the platform handles the money.
results.finding: The section's only sentence stacks three scope qualifiers and three claims; both readers had to parse it twice (reader A: 'It is convoluted: one sentence stacks three scope qualifiers and three claims'). The prose can state the same controlling idea in two plain sentences.

results.draft_locus: The Digital Services Act as a Set of System Requirements ¶13
results.quote: Veldmark's report for 2027, published in February 2028, was the first produced this way: the evidence store held decision, notice, complaint and enforcement events
results.finding: The scene says the shared platform 'went live for Tradeyard Netherlands and Belgium in November 2027'; this paragraph says the whole-year 2027 report for all three platforms was computed from that evidence store. Reader A: 'I re-read both passages to work out how events from January to October 2027, and from Motorvane and Hearthly, got into a store that went live in November'. Both facts are in the spec's scenario evidence (p08, p28), so the conflict must be resolved in the spec/ledger (e.g. a backfill, or a different first reproducible year) before the prose can.

results.quote: For the phishing account's suspension at 20:26 on 7 March 2027, the decision record names the confirming analyst and policy `POL-FRAUD-PAYLINK` version 2
results.finding: The DSA section presents this decision as a counterfactual ('Had the November 2027 pipeline existed then, the decision record would carry ...'); the close states it as an actual record with a submission and a saved query. Both readers stopped to check whether the decision went through the new pipeline. The close can keep the callback while saying the test is answered as the decision would run on the records Part V built.

results.quote: Four overlapping sources, five rules in all, regulate how a marketplace orders and labels what users see. Read together, they ask for three disclosure surfaces; P2B and Omnibus rules then reach seller tooling, price badges and reviews.
results.finding: Both readers had to count table rows to reconcile 'four sources' with 'five rules', and the clause after the semicolon compresses three later topics into one phrase that was only understood after reading the section (reader A, item A4).

results.draft_locus: Beyond the EU: UK and US Rules in Brief ¶3
results.quote: INFORM repeats the DAC7 pattern, so **the decision to launch in-platform payments is also a regulatory decision**, outside the EU as well as inside it: under the US INFORM Consumers Act, only sales made through the marketplace with payment processed by it count toward the high-volume seller threshold.
results.finding: The conclusion comes before its reason, which is appended after a colon; both readers read the sentence twice (reader A, item A6). Putting the marketplace-processed-sales fact first and the conclusion after it keeps the controlling idea and fixes the read.

results.draft_locus: DAC7: When Payments Turn a Marketplace into a Tax Reporter ¶2
results.quote: The definition of "platform" carries the exclusion that matters most for classifieds
results.finding: Reader A (item A5): the point the section itself calls most important for classifieds comes after the full definitions list (activities, consideration, thresholds, reported fields, deadlines), so the reader works through thresholds before learning whether a classifieds site is in scope. The order p40 then p41 is the spec's. Reported by one reader only.

results.quote: Beyond its ranking rule, the P2B Regulation adds two process rules for business users that belong in the professional-seller platform.
results.finding: Reader B (item B6): notice periods for terms changes and dealer termination are not about ranking, advertising or consumer transparency and felt out of place under that heading. The placement is the spec's (p32 in the transparency section). Reported by one reader only.

results.quote: As of October 2026, the Commission has proposed repealing the P2B Regulation
results.finding: Reader B (item B3): the story is told in the past tense up to the February 2028 report, but this paragraph and the role table speak from October 2026, so the reader had to reorient. The 'as of October 2026' framing is fixed in the spec's p65. Reported by one reader only.

results.quote: Every cross-brand decision record that touches a regulated capability cites the obligations it affects.
results.finding: Reader B (item B10): throughout the chapter 'decision record' means the moderation decision record; here it apparently means an architecture decision record, and the reader first read it in the moderation sense. Naming it (e.g. 'architecture decision record') removes the collision. Reported by one reader only.

results.quote: [[trust-and-safety-architecture]] owns the moderation pipeline, the decision service and enforcement propagation. [[identity-and-verification]] owns identity levels, KYB and the business registry.
results.finding: Reader B (item B5): ¶4 mostly repeats ¶3's pointer to the same two chapters and delays the roadmap; the reader re-read to see what it added. Reported by one reader only.
